text: Consider following JSON Schema: , id required field serves unique user assignment record. create records comply schema, create following records: retrieve JSON schema definition data warehouse, can make request /api/warehouse/data-sources/{uuid}/ endpoint, uuid uuid target data source. schema definition located head_primary_definition$schema field response.
code: {   "title": "A registration form",   "description": "A simple form example.",   "type": "object",   "required": [     "id",     "firstName",     "lastName"   ],   "properties": {     "id": {       "type": "string",       "title": "ID"     },     "firstName": {       "type": "string",       "title": "First name",       "default": "Chuck"     },     "lastName": {       "type": "string",       "title": "Last name",       "default": "Norris"     },     "age": {       "type": "integer",       "title": "Age"     },     "telephone": {       "type": "string",       "title": "Telephone",       "minLength": 10     }   } } records <- list(   list(id = "xxxx", firstName = "John", lastName = "Doe", age = 30, telephone = "1234567890"),   list(id = "yyyy", firstName = "Jane", lastName = "Smith", age = 25, telephone = "0987654321") ) data_source <- make_request(   endpoint = paste0("api/warehouse/data-sources/", Sys.getenv("SOURCE_UUID")) )  schema <- data_source$head_primary_definition$schema

title: CSIAPPS REST API
text: can validate data records using jsonlite jsonvalidate packages. sure set auto_unbox = TRUE converting JSON objects strings. Finally, can make API request ingest records warehouse:
code: json_schema <- jsonvalidate::json_schema$new(jsonlite::toJSON(schema, auto_unbox = T))  validate_record <- function(record) {   json_schema$validate(jsonlite::toJSON(record, auto_unbox = T)) }  validation_results <- sapply(records, validate_record)  stopifnot(all(validation_results)) result <- make_request(   endpoint = "api/warehouse/ingestion/primary/",   method = "POST",   body = list(     source = Sys.getenv("SOURCE_UUID"),     records = records,     subject_field = "id"   ) )

title: Developing Shiny Web Applications
text: Suppose following shiny web application: migrate app within CSIAPPS ecosystem, can leverage several functions provided csiapps.
code: library(shiny)  df = faithful[, 2]  ui <- fluidPage(      titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),      sidebarLayout(         sidebarPanel(             sliderInput("bins",                         "Number of bins:",                         min = 1,                         max = 50,                         value = 30)         ),          mainPanel(            plotOutput("distPlot")         )     ) )  server <- function(input, output) {      output$distPlot <- renderPlot({         bins <- seq(min(df), max(df), length.out = input$bins + 1)          hist(df, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white',              xlab = 'Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)',              main = 'Histogram of waiting times')     }) }  shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

title: Developing Shiny Web Applications
text: Therefore, full code app, migration, look like :
code: library(shiny) library(csiapps)  # CSIAPPS Setup set_institute("csiontario") check_secrets()  global_wrapper({   df = faithful[, 2] })  # Define UI for application that draws a histogram ui <- fluidPage(      titlePanel("Old Faithful Geyser Data"),      sidebarLayout(         sidebarPanel(             sliderInput("bins",                         "Number of bins:",                         min = 1,                         max = 50,                         value = 30)         ),          mainPanel(            plotOutput("distPlot")         )     ) )  # Define server logic required to draw a histogram server <- function(input, output) {      output$distPlot <- renderPlot({         bins <- seq(min(df), max(df), length.out = input$bins + 1)          # draw the histogram with the specified number of bins         hist(df, breaks = bins, col = 'darkgray', border = 'white',              xlab = 'Waiting time to next eruption (in mins)',              main = 'Histogram of waiting times')     }) }  # Run the application shinyApp(ui = ui_wrapper(ui), server = server_wrapper(server))

what: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: Sandbox mode lets developers run full schema -> validate -> ingest -> retrieve warehouse workflow entirely locally, network access authentication. Sandbox mode enabled default, development work never reaches production warehouse accident: make_request() calls routed local, -memory warehouse instead REST API. disabled deployment options(csiapps.sandbox = FALSE) (setting CSIAPPS_ENV=production), can overridden per call sandbox argument make_request(). production sandbox workflows use calls, code changes needed moving development deployment. sandbox emulates three endpoints: GET api/warehouse/data-sources/{uuid} – returns schema previously registered register_sandbox_schema(), nested head_primary_definition$schema exactly like real API. POST api/warehouse/ingestion/primary/ – validates body$records registered schema body$source (using jsonvalidate) , success, stores memory writes JSON payload per-source folder disk inspection (see browse_sandbox()). GET api/warehouse/data-records – returns previously ingested records query$source_uuid, wrapped envelope (data, subject, created_at, ...) real API returns. endpoint raises error. Sandbox state lasts R session; use clear_sandbox() reset tests.

title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: Sandbox mode also lets wrapped Shiny app (see ui_wrapper(), server_wrapper(), check_secrets()) run locally without OAuth2 redirect. redirect exists obtain access token, requires client credentials safely distributed, sandbox mode server_wrapper() simulates login instead: seeds session developer's existing CSIAPPS_ACCESS_TOKEN hands code path production login . token present, /organization list loaded real registration API, developer sees real identity organizations. token set, app shell still renders shows unauthenticated notice prompting developer set read-CSIAPPS_ACCESS_TOKEN. wrapped-app code therefore runs modes; csiapps.sandbox option differs.

title: Sandbox mode for local development — csiapps-sandbox
text: Sandbox fully offline wrapped apps. Warehouse endpoints routed make_request() emulated locally, wrapper's registration reads (/, organizations, profiles) bypass make_request() call real API token. Sandbox mode thus deliberately split: warehouse data emulated, registration/auth data real. Set institute set_institute() match institute issued token, reads rejected. sandbox faithfully simulates schema contract, warehouse. Anything depends server-side state differ production: Validation parity approximate. Sandbox ingestion validates records JSON Schema Ajv (via jsonvalidate), catches common failure modes (missing required fields, wrong types, length pattern violations). real server additionally enforces things schema express: resolution subject_field values registered profiles, duplicate/dataset handling existing data, token permissions. Validator implementations may also differ edge cases (e.g. format keyword enforcement). Passing sandbox validation therefore necessary sufficient condition production acceptance – treat green sandbox run guarantee. subject always NULL retrieved records. production server links ingested record registered profile returns (name, sport, ...) record envelope. sandbox profile registry, emulate linkage returns subject = NULL rather fabricating misleading data. Code displays filters subject fields see placeholder values, mistyped subject_field values production flag accepted silently.
